ai.description: *Cristidorsa otai* reaches 8–10 cm in snout-vent length. It is olive-brown with a distinct, serrated crest along the nape and back. A prominent, pale-edged dark patch marks the side of the neck.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cristidorsa otai* is best distinguished by the presence of a prominent, continuous crest of elongated scales along the nape and back, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Cristidorsa otai* inhabits the high-altitude evergreen forests and shola grasslands of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Ota’s Mountain Lizard is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small insects and invertebrates among the rocky outcrops and vegetation of its high-altitude habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cristidorsa otai* is oviparous, laying a clutch of 4–6 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cristidorsa otai* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats of India, specifically inhabiting high-elevation shola forests and grasslands in Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
